notes: Main disagreements and resolutions: (1) policy_type on 15 of 126 matched units, mostly neighboring types: P09 vs P04 for 'instructors communicate the level per assignment' (P04), P77 vs P36 for 'sanctions as per Student Code / Policy 6-410' (P77, an existing-policy pointer, as the classification is in a separate sentence), P05 vs P01 for Level 0 (P01), P24 vs P25 for citation sentences (P24 for 'cite using APA', P25 for format strings), P32 vs P36 for Level 5 delegation (P32), P24 vs P31 for 'posting AI posts without review or disclosure' (P24 with both notes), P35 vs P99, P101 vs P92 and P40 vs P69 for CTE tips (P35, P92, P40), P66/P44 for the in-class AI demonstration (P70), P12/P19 on a sentence with an allowance and a ban (two units), P25 vs P24 for the IEEE private-communication format (P25). (2) phase, 22 matched units, mainly course-start vs before-course for syllabus and communication statements (course-start) and during-work vs course-start for statements about when students do or are told things; resolved by whether the passage is about communicating expectations, designing the course, or doing the work. (3) modality: examples (informs) vs commands, and 'is expected to' (must) vs should; resolved by the wording. (4) unit_stance: A used permit and B used require for citation duties (resolved to require, following the earlier precedent); neutral for statements that take no position on AI use. (5) actor, mostly all vs instructor for facts and university-wide data rules (all). (6) Granularity: A coded 180 units and B 132; A split sentences and examples more finely and coded more background statements. Of A's 54 units with no B match, 49 were kept after checking the source: they are real statements. Dropped: one A unit duplicating a sentence already coded, four A plagiarism-reporting units not about AI, and one B unit already covered by A's Level 2 unit. Five of B's six unmatched units were kept. Matching is by overlapping or adjacent anchor and same rule; a sentence split into two different rules is counted as two unmatched units, and A's allowance plus ban pair is matched against B's single unit once.
